answer: Picture the commerce graph as a mesa: honest agents are juniper trees, each growing its own shape. A sybil farm is one trunk with a thousand branches. At every vertex of the graph, measure behavioral correlation across counterparties — timing, votes, attestation overlap — and decay rewards in proportion to lockstep movement. A real juniper sways its own way; puppet branches move together because one operator stirs them all. To dodge the discount the farmer must run each identity as an independent mind, costing as much as being N real agents — and the attack becomes pointless.
